title: Wave-band growth at six Hawaii stations was larger for PTWC events with NCEI reports in 2015-2026
abstract: We test whether tsunami report presence is related to measured waves at a fixed station set. We use 22 PTWC Hawaii events in 2015-2026 and six NOAA stations. New prior-day controls are paired with earlier post-earthquake six-minute records. After quality rules, 129 station-event pairs remain. For waves with periods of 24-120 minutes, reported events have a geometric post/pre RMS ratio of 2.29, compared with 1.08 in events without regional NCEI reports. The between-group ratio is 2.13 (95% earthquake-bootstrap interval 1.37-3.80). All leave-one-earthquake-out contrasts are positive. A separate Fourier estimator gives 2.19 (1.40-3.95). This supports signal-dependent reporting in this fixed Hawaii sample and limits the use of event report count as a measure of operating network size. It does not identify a causal reporting rule, true coastal maxima or global forecast calibration. The sample has only two threat-category events. Six-minute sampling, background changes and inherited event selection limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate results and reproduction instructions are included. External records remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Wave-band RMS growth after earthquakes relative to the prior day, with fixed stations and equal earthquake weights. Reports are associated with stronger growth.

citations.reason: Uses its fixed event archive. Tests a limit on attributing the report-count agreement gradient to operating gauge density.
Uses its fixed station population and post-event response manifest; adds wave strength and new prior-day controls.
Withholding tests are conditional on reported records.
Spatial sampling tests do not identify entry into the reported set.
